referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, so a canopy grid lands two by two on the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles. Nothing on it opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches to it -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides: no walls, no infill, no hanging goods. Market rows, food courts, bus stops and yard shelters across rural and peri-urban Thailand; a row of bays butted post to post is what a covered market is. Silver-brown sawn hardwood gone grey, palm thatch bleaching from tan to straw and blackening in the course shadows.

reasoning: ONE timber merge -- four posts, two plates, two tie beams, eight knee braces, two king posts, the ridge beam, the ridge plank, eight rafters and twelve cord lashings; ONE thatch height grid carrying both slopes and the torn fringe on all four edges; ONE InstancedMesh of eight purlins: THREE draw calls of 4.
Two materials of three: sawn timber (vertex colours -- post, plate, rafter, ridge plank, cord) and thatch. Both textureless, each with one post-construction canvas.
Repetition system: the purlin is the one part repeated at a fixed station, eight of them at four heights on each slope.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: At distance the identity is a deep-eaved thatched gable standing well proud of four inset posts, with a torn fringe on every edge; close up it is the course structure of the thatch and the tied post-and-plate frame under it. The registry notes forbid modelled fronds, so the courses are a canvas and the fringe is real geometry -- a per-column drop in the height grid's eave rows and a per-row drop in its verge columns, which is the one place a flat roof reads as thatch.

resolvedUnknowns: The roof stops ON the module edge and the POSTS are inset 0.45 m to give it the plate's overhang. The plate and the proxy both show a freestanding shelter with a deep eave; a 4 m grid bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour, so the overhang is bought inside the cell, and two butted bays stand their posts 0.90 m apart under one roof.

The eave is the thatch TOP surface at 2.20 m rather than the notes' 2.40: the notes' figure is a clearance figure, and the clearance is under the head frame (1.98 m) at the post line, which the lower eave does not touch. It buys 24.9 degrees of pitch against 18.3, and the arithmetic is in envelopeDerivation and on the asset notes.
The ridge is capped by a sawn plank, as the plate shows, not by a rolled thatch ridge; the plank's top IS the declared height.
Purlins run along the ridge on top of the rafters and are only visible from underneath and through the open gable ends; the plate shows them there.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the ridge along X. A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z with the same alignment; its roof meets this one edge to edge and its posts stand 0.90 m from these, so a row reads as one continuous roof on paired posts.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 150 mm posts at +-1.55 m carrying plates at 1.98-2.12 m and tie beams at 2.12-2.24 m with eight short knee braces and rope lashings, a 24.9 degree gable above them with its ridge along X and 0.45 m of overhang on every side, thatch 180 mm thick from a 2.20 m eave to a 3.13 m apex, a sawn ridge plank capping it at 3.20 m, and a torn fringe hanging up to 0.42 m below the eave line and 0.32 m below the verges. Open on all four sides. Height revision 2026-09-27: all historical roof/frame Y coordinates above are raised by 1.10 m; ground posts lengthened by 1.10 m; foot hardware and tarpaulin bottom rails stay grounded. Exact revised construction is in canopyHeightRefinement.geometry.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span exactly -2.000..+2.000 and nothing crosses it: the thatch owns the module edge, and the frame sits INSIDE it -- post centres at +-1.550, plate and tie-beam ends at +-1.770, ridge beam and ridge plank 20 mm short, and the ROTATED rafter boxes 50 mm short because a box turned about X has an AABB half-depth of L/2 cos(s) + h/2 sin(s). Clean at 0.001 m in check-coplanar. y 0.000 to 3.200 at the top of the ridge plank. Proxy (Meshy v7): w:h:d 1 : 1.146 : 1.216, a SQUARE post grid of 0.769 x 0.765 H under a roof of 0.810 x 1.011 H, ridge along the narrow axis -- so the proxy overhangs its post grid by 0.121 H (0.39 m) at the eaves, and the plate shows the same deep eave and verge with rafter and purlin ends visible under it. The first build put the posts on the cell edge and had no overhang; this build keeps the ROOF on the cell edge (the grid is the contract) and moves the posts IN: post grid / roof span 3.10 / 4.00 = 0.775 against the proxy's 0.765 / 1.011 = 0.757. Eave height: the notes' 2.40 was written for clearance, and clearance is needed under the HEAD FRAME at the post line, not under the eave edge, which a player only meets from outside where the plate's fringe hangs lower still. Eave top 2.20 over a 2.00 run gives 24.9 degrees against the proxy's 39 (the first build's 18.3); thatch top at the post line 3.13 - 0.775 x 0.93 = 2.41, underside 2.23, tie beams 2.12-2.24, plates 1.98-2.12, posts to 1.98: 1.98 m of headroom everywhere inside the frame. Post section from the proxy: 4 of 100 occupancy columns = 0.052 H = 0.166 m, built 0.150.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1 : 1.146 : 1.216, post grid 0.769 x 0.765 H, roof 0.810 x 1.011 H, eave at 0.61 H, pitch 39 degrees. Used for the POST SECTION (0.052 H = 0.166 m), for the post-grid-to-roof ratio (0.757, built 0.775) and for confirming that the post grid is square and the ridge runs across the narrow axis. NOT used for the eave height: the 3.20 m ridge is declared and the eave is set by walk-under clearance under the head frame, so the built pitch is 24.9 degrees against the proxy's 39. The arithmetic is in envelopeDerivation.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the bay is symmetric about both axes and open on all four sides, so the far side is the near side; the plate shows one gable end and one eave, which between them cover every distinct elevation.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 4.000 x 3.200 x 4.000 m off the built module, nothing crossing the cell edge on either axis; four 150 mm posts at +-1.550 under a roof that owns +-2.000, so the eave and the verge overhang the post line by 0.45 m the way the plate and the proxy (0.121 H) show; plates 1.98-2.12, tie beams 2.12-2.24, eave 2.20, thatch apex 3.13, ridge plank top 3.200; a 24.9 degree gable with the ridge along X; open on all four sides. Post grid / roof span 0.775 against the proxy's 0.757.

Whole-asset visual review: correct raised head frame; the fringe remains too tooth-like with deep isolated notches. Reduce isolated fringe extrema while retaining torn palm-leaf silhouette.

Full visual fidelity target confirmed by user. Replace synthetic roof finish with de-lit reference-relative albedo and independent inferred roughness/normal maps; source crop checked and extraction confidence >=0.7. Preserve authored palette and raised geometry.

Rejected small-crop tiling candidate: repeated marks and over-strong inferred normals lower fidelity. Use a rectified complete roof face once per slope, mild independent normals, and absolute albedo; retain failed renders as evidence.

Whole-face material preserves reference wear layout, but shader lighting overexposes the inferred albedo. Apply a neutral per-material transfer correction; keep hue, PBR channels and spatial marks unchanged.

Roof projection now retains all admitted material pixels; the old object-background segmentation had incorrectly erased pale fibre and zinc. Next replace blocky frame weathering with an inspected full post crop, orient timber grain along each member, and retain measured palette.
Taper the last 0.35 m of the nipa shell from 180 mm bulk to an 18 mm leaf edge, eliminating the block-like cut rim while keeping the torn silhouette.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components plus one repetition system: 3 of 4.

materials.note: timber and thatch: 2 of 3. Post, plate, brace, rafter, ridge plank and cord are vertex colours on one material, not six.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,120 of 4,000: 480 in the frame merge (40 boxes), 2,544 in the thatch height grid (two 48 x 12 smooth grids plus four wound edge strips -- the fringe is bought with grid density), 96 in eight purlin instances.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes throughout the frame, several rotated onto the 45 degree braces and the 24.9 degree rafter slope; the roof is a height grid with thickness.
One InstancedMesh of eight purlins. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid; the module does not repeat itself.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases after construction, ~2 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The eave is built at 2.20 m against the registry notes' 2.40, and the fringe hangs to ~1.60 m at the cell edge; the notes' 2.40 was a clearance figure.
risks.mitigation: Clearance is measured where a player actually walks: under the head frame at the post line, 1.98 m, and the eave edge is 0.45 m OUTSIDE the posts where a player meets it only from the open side. The pitch it buys (24.9 against 18.3, plate 39) is most of what the first build lacked. Recorded on the asset notes with the arithmetic.

risks.description: Even at 24.9 degrees the roof is shallower than the plate's ~39; the ridge is declared at 3.20 and cannot rise.
risks.mitigation: The gable is unambiguous at azimuth 90 and 270; a steeper roof would need either a higher ridge (a declaration change) or an eave under 1.98 m, which fails the headroom the notes exist for.

risks.description: The bay is open on all four sides, so most of what the silhouette encloses is background: the volume under the roof, both gable voids, and the bays between the knee braces; the dark thatch underside seen through the gables is deliberately close to the plate's #4a4036 and sits inside the outline.
risks.mitigation: The turntable gate is run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement, and holeviz was read per azimuth to confirm the red covers the open volume and never a solid surface. Every timber face was lifted off the backdrop band first (darkest 94 against 58) so no solid part of the prop can be classified as a hole.
